speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (a) how will the substantial emissions from the new coal gasification plant on Jurong Island align with our climate change commitments and our declaration of Year of Climate Action; and (b) how does the Government decide on business opportunities versus environmental concerns and international commitments.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: A lower emissions intensity means that each dollar of gross domestic product (GDP) will be achieved more efficiently and with a lower impact to the environment.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: With 2018 designated as the Year of Climate Action, the Government will increase efforts to raise awareness and increase involvement of companies and individuals on the necessity and the benefits of taking action to achieve sustainable growth and move towards a low-carbon future.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One is, how will the substantive amount of ash be disposed of, specifically the fly ash, as this is known to be hazardous?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Second, which is important, is how do we reconcile the different messages we are sending to the public now?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: On one hand, we are saying it is a Year of Climate Action to reduce our carbon footprint but, on the other hand, we are opening up this coal gasification plant which will increase our carbon footprint?

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: On reconciling the two, this is a delicate balance that we have to try to achieve.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: We have to maintain the competitiveness of that sector and, for that, we need competitive feedstock – hydrogen and carbon monoxide.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: We have explored the different ways of introducing that feedstock and gasification appears to be the most sensible approach.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: So, in balancing the two, we have reached an agreement with the operator on the regulations that they have to meet, both in carbon dioxide emissions as well as in other standards.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: And they have agreed to deploy best-in-class technologies.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Could I check where would the ash be disposed of?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: The second question is whether we considered renewable energy instead.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Minister Ong Ye Kung has replied to the earlier Parliamentary Question about how that is a growing sector and whether the Ministry of Trade and Industry will consider that instead of this coal gasification plant.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: It is to produce hydrogen and carbon monoxide or, essentially, carbon.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: Because as feedstock to the petrochemical sector, you need more C and more H2.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: And to do that, you need to convert coal into hydrogen and carbon monoxide.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: Because we are not adding on to refineries in Singapore, we have 1.3 million barrels of refining capacity and that has not changed for many decades, so we need additional feedstock from other sources.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: Therefore, we have looked towards gasification of coal.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: I want to assure Members here that, in terms of energy generation, we are still depending on natural gas which is the least pollutive of all and, of course, supplemented by solar energy in a limited way.
